theme: ज्ञान-दीप्त कर्म; desireless action, freedom without grasp.
context: In the preceding verses, Krishna has described sacrifice, wisdom, and the discipline of selfless action. He continues that teaching here, describing a wise person whose undertakings are free from desire and whose actions are burned by the fire of knowledge.
contextHindi: पिछले श्लोकों में श्रीकृष्ण ने यज्ञ, ज्ञान और निष्काम कर्म की बात की है। यहाँ वे अपनी शिक्षा आगे बढ़ाते हैं। वे ऐसे ज्ञानी का वर्णन करते हैं, जिसके काम कामना से मुक्त हैं और जिसके कर्म ज्ञान की अग्नि में जल चुके हैं।
sanskritDevanagari:
यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः |
ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः ||४-१९||
transliteration:
yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāmasaṅkalpavarjitāḥ .
jñānāgnidagdhakarmāṇaṃ tamāhuḥ paṇḍitaṃ budhāḥ ||4-19||

wordByWord.meaning: whose; for one whose inner life is being described.
all undertakings; every effort and initiative.
free from desire and self-willed purpose; not driven by craving or egoic intention.
whose actions are burned by the fire of knowledge; purified by insight rather than by mere outward effort.
the learned one; the wise people call such a person a real knower.

spokenHindi: यहाँ श्रीकृष्ण बताते हैं कि ज्ञानी किसे कहते हैं। उसके सभी काम कामना और संकल्प से मुक्त होते हैं। यानी वह लालच या अपने स्वार्थी इरादे से काम नहीं करता। श्लोक कहता है कि उसके कर्म ज्ञान की अग्नि में जले हुए हैं। ‘ज्ञानाग्नि’ का सीधा अर्थ है ज्ञान की अग्नि। यहाँ ज्ञान केवल पढ़ी हुई बातों तक सीमित नहीं है; आत्मज्ञान से व्यक्ति कर्म को अपना बताकर उससे चिपकना छोड़ता है। ऐसे कर्म का बंधनकारी असर मिट जाता है। इसलिए ज्ञानी को केवल बहुत पढ़ा हुआ व्यक्ति नहीं कहा गया है। बुद्धिमान लोग उसे पण्डित कहते हैं, क्योंकि उसके काम में समझ और आसक्ति से मुक्ति दिखाई देती है। इसका अर्थ यह नहीं कि वह काम करना छोड़ देता है। वह अपना काम करता है, लेकिन फल को पाने की लालसा या ‘मैं ही सब कर रहा हूँ’ के भाव से नहीं।
clearEnglish: Krishna defines the truly wise person not by intellectual display but by the character of action. All undertakings are free from kāma-saṅkalpa, meaning desire and self-constructed purpose. That is not a moralistic slogan; it is a description of inner freedom. When a person acts without the urge to possess outcomes, the action is no longer a chain. The “fire of knowledge” here is not only book learning but the insight that the self is not a small ego seeking gain. That insight burns the fuel of karma, because the fuel is attachment, self-claim, and the urge to control the result. The wise person is therefore not a withdrawn renunciate; the wise person is one whose action is clear, disciplined, and non-possessive. The criterion is inward freedom, not outer busyness.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse plainly states that one whose undertakings are free from desire and self-willed purpose, and whose actions are consumed by the fire of knowledge, is called a learned person.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: This does not require inactivity; it points to an inner shift in which action continues but the egoic claim on results is reduced. In practice, the core issue is not whether we work, but whether the work binds us.

practicalApplication.label: Pause before action
practicalApplication.text: Before starting a task, ask: am I acting from clarity or from craving for praise, control, or reward? Let the answer shape the effort.

practicalApplication.label: Release the result
practicalApplication.text: During the day, notice the urge to evaluate each outcome immediately. Practice doing the work well, then returning attention to the next task rather than the next reward.

reflectionQuestion: When you feel compelled to act, what part of the urge is desire for the result rather than care for the task itself?
reflectionQuestionHindi: जब आप कुछ करने के लिए आग्रह महसूस करते हैं, तो वह इच्छा परिणाम की ओर है या काम की शुद्धता की ओर?
